reports.title: Andersen Group Reports Third Quarter Revenue Growth of 18.7% to $337.3 Million

desk.headline: Revenue up 18.7% to $337.3m, above estimates; GAAP loss per share on IPO-related costs; 2026 outlook raised and 2027 revenue guided to $1.275–1.325bn

numbers.eps_basis: GAAP net loss per Class A share, basic and diluted (no prior-year figure: company listed in Dec 2025)

results: Revenue rose 18.7% to $337.3m, with every service line and region growing; new international acquisitions added $10.7m.
Adjusted EBITDA grew 18.8% to $154.5m with a steady 45.8% margin, but adjusted net income fell 8.3% to $115.7m on higher tax and interest after the IPO.
On a GAAP basis the listed company lost $9.0m ($0.55 a Class A share), mainly because most profit is allocated to partners' minority interests and $47.5m of share-based pay was expensed.
Eight acquisitions closed by 30 September, adding about $37.2m of yearly revenue for roughly $25.0m; many more deals are signed for Q4 and Q1 2027.
Nine-month operating cash flow was $142.8m and the firm had $193.6m in cash with no bank borrowings.

guidance.summary: Andersen gave its first 2027 outlook: revenue of $1.275–1.325bn (about 30% growth at the midpoint) and adjusted EBITDA of $320–340m. Call coverage reports it also raised its 2026 revenue and adjusted EBITDA ranges.

points: Organic growth was about 15%, with revenue per person up 14.6% and year-to-date client groups up 24%.
Management cited 24 deals signed since March, 16 closed, and said its acquired-revenue estimate looks conservative.
Acquired firms earn lower margins (15–25%), so a bigger acquisition mix will dilute margins unless organic growth offsets it.
Management described its 2027 targets as conservative.
call.source: Call coverage: Earnings Whispers via Finviz, 12 Nov 2026 (no prepared remarks filed)

watch: Integration of the many deals closing in Q4 2026 and Q1 2027, and their effect on margins.
Whether organic growth holds near mid-teens as staff attrition (15.8%) edges up.
The gap between strong adjusted profit and GAAP results while IPO-related share pay continues.

sources.title: Andersen Misses On GAAP Optics But Raises 2026 Guidance And Sets A 30% Growth Target For 2027 As Deal Activity Accelerates — Earnings Whispers via Finviz, 12 Nov 2026
